This is really an innovative game. I've been playing for over 4 hours and had to force myself to call it a night finally because it's so late. It's actually a pretty long game if you're like me and really dive into all of the things available to access.

The characters are really interesting. I didn't expect to get invested in anyone and am very pleasantly surprised. There's so many dialogue options that it keeps you drawn in at all times. 

Probably my favorite aspect is the attention to detail. You can look at different web pages for example and actually click on and access a lot of areas you wouldn't have expected. I found myself spending a lot of time just having fun with this aspect and got sidetracked for a while just seeing what all I could access and do. 

As I said, I've yet to finish but am having a blast so far. I'm actually surprised at the price considering its quality. I highly recommend everyone give this a try if you want to just be really immersed in a unique game.

Okay, so i just finished playing this (took me something like 5 or 6 hours I believe), and I felt compelled to review this game because it's like nothing I've played before. I had never heard of the "found-phone" genre in games before.

First let me say this: if you're a fan of mysteries, riddles, horror, or to be more specific, found-footage horror, then this game is for you! If not, try it anyway lol you just might be surprised.

This game starts out with you booting up a phone that was sent to you (or left on your doorstep, it's not totally cleared up in the story), and when you do it begins to glitch out a little and then these texts start coming in, and well, it just takes off from there...

The basic premise is that the owner of the phone, a girl named Anna, has gone missing and it's up to you (and a couple others along the way) to try to find her. You do this by digging through her phone and reading EVERYTHING, and then communicating with some of her contacts through texts and emails and an online dating app and a twitter-like app.  As things progress you learn that she has dissapeared and it may be connected to other recent dissapearances (but I won't go into more on that because I don't want to ruin the experience for new players).  Eventually, you realize there's a lot more going on than meets the eye.

The game has a very unnerving, intense feeling to it, and is all the better for it.  It has a decent story, some fun little mini games and riddles, a good amount of investigation and some pretty convinging dialogues, and for the REALLY hardcore sleuths out there, it even has some very interesting "easter eggs" hidden in the game that are quite rewarding to find. (I'll give you a hint here, but that's it...morse code, click it :)   )

As for graphics, sound, story, gameplay, etc...well graphics aren't important here as it's basically a phone emulator, the gameplay is as simple as digging through a phone and talking to people and looking stuff up (but you need a brain lol), the story is interesting enough that you really will never get bored in a single playthrough, and apparently it has many different endings so it has replayability there...where this game really shines though is the sound...it's incredible and really really well done.  When you start they recommend you use headphones, and I STRONGLY recommend you take their advice, it's just not the same on speakers, not even close

Anyway, the TL;DR is this:
if you 're looking for an action title, look elsewhere, but if you're looking for an EXPERIENCE that really makes you feel like you're a part of a mystery that needs to be solved, I can't recommend this highly enough. It's fun as hell!

Oh man. How do I even start? This game was very, very intense. Definitely creepy and super interesting. I don't tend to do horror games, but this one seemed like one that could really deliver. 

 If you've read the premise, you know it's about trying to find the owner of the "lost" phone you've somehow come in possession of. I really like the use of technology is this story. It's set up so that the player is essentially working through a cell phone. There are all kinds of ethical situations you find yourself in as well as interacting with the people in this missing person's life. Who do you trust? Who do you tell? Why is crazy stuff starting to happen? It's all really well done. 

Besides the acting being a bit over the top at times and occasionally not having a respose available that I would have liked, this game delivers rather well. It was suspenseful but humorous in places so that it wasn't totally overwhleming. The story's end was a surprise, which was nice. I thought it was well worth the price. Furthermore, it even has a NG+ that lets you speed through the texts faster so that you can try other paths. I have fully completed the game in about 8.5 hours, which may seem short, but it was so enjoyable that I didn't seem to notice. 

I highly recommend this game and look forward to what the developers decide to release next.

An extremely interesting experience that goes a bit south near the end. 

Simulacra takes place entirely on the phone of Anna, a missing young woman. The player is in posession of her phone, trying to solve the mystery of her disappearance by talking to her friends and enemies, and logging into her various social media accounts. You never know who you can trust, and there's a menacing supernatural element in the background that builds suspense. 

This is all extremely compelling, and it was hard to stop playing- however once the truth is revealed and you come face to face with what's responsible, it takes you right out of the game. It's not enough to tarnish the whole experience, but I really wish they had gone in a different direction.

You can replay the game for alternate ending sequences and achievements but the overall story will not change drastically, still it might add in some additional hours of play for completionists.

Despite what I consider a disappointing conclusion, I strongly recommend playing through this.

I really don't like Steam's binary review system. I feel like "some" people would like this game... but to me it's suffering the following:

[list]
[*]Imbalance between (unintended?) camp and "horror" (mostly to do with a couple V/O performances)
[*]EXTREME over-reliance on jump-scares (which takes away from the investigation/mystery aspect)
[*]Some rough writing here and there
[*]Some "simulated choice" options (i.e. you HAVE to say things even if you wouldn't want to or it wouldn't make sense for your character to)
[*]Some REALLY obscure puzzles that have had to be answered by the developers themselves

All-in-all it's not a "bad" game... but it's a great "idea" with some execution misses.

That being said, if you love jump-scares and some weird screwed up imagery with "INTENSE" sound effects, etc. then you might dig this. If I were to arm-chair develop this, I would have held back on some of the jump scares to make them more effective than just annyoing, and leaned more into the "missing person investigation" aspect of things vs. bringing in the [spoiler]supernatural[/spoiler] elements so quickly. 

I think the overall presentation and mechanics are solid... none of my critiques of this game are "budget-related," but more about writing/pacing/etc. 

I'm gonna give this a "no" but with a big caveat, that I wouldn't recommend it to MOST people... I really think something special and unique is buried under the surface of this game, but I think maybe the development team just got a little to shy of the story itself and decided to overload it with trope-y jumpscare image-horror to cover it up a bit. 

I know these games are made by real people, and I empathize with the team behind this and hope they know that my "negative" review comes with a healthy does of optimisim that they have something great in them and look forward to their next go of it!
